pages.headline: The contractor marks the job complete. The account manager calls the site because the docket, client sign-off and invoice still do not agree.
pages.body: A completed job waiting to bill. An inspection without accepted evidence. Extra work awaiting approval. An urgent job with conflicting clocks. Planned maintenance displaced by callouts. A contractor blocked at the gate. Each needs contract context, proof from the responsible party and an authorized disposition. Orcaworks coordinates the handoffs across client portals, FM systems, procurement and email.
pages.callout: FM leaders face steady workload growth supported by modest budgets and constrained staffing
pages.calloutSource: Nickalos Rocha, IFMA · FM Pulse Report, 2026

pages.eyebrow: 01 / Service delivery · Completed job to approved billing
pages.title: Completion-to-invoice evidence
pages.problem: The work order is closed, but the contractor’s invoice does not match the attendance record, approved quote or client sign-off. The account team calls the site and searches email for the missing docket or variation approval. Finance keeps the invoice on hold while supplier payment and the provider’s own client billing wait.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks assembles the job, quote, purchase order, service evidence and invoice into one exception case. The responsible client or account owner accepts the service evidence; finance approves eligible billing or payment, and the permitted posting or reasoned hold is recorded.

pages.eyebrow: 02 / Asset assurance · Job completion to accepted certificate
pages.title: Statutory service evidence
pages.problem: A planned inspection appears complete, yet its certificate is missing, names the wrong asset or omits the service period and signature. The facilities coordinator checks the asset register, service report and contractor replies. The responsible technical reviewer still needs valid evidence and a clear disposition for any defects before accepting the record.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks matches required inspection evidence to the asset, service period and qualified provider, then requests the exact correction. The competent reviewer and responsible client authority accept the evidence or retain an owned defect and follow-up before the register changes.

rightContent.alt: Inspector with a tablet and manager reviewing stock in a warehouse aisle

pages.eyebrow: 03 / Extra works · Proposed scope to client authorization
pages.title: Variation approval packs
pages.problem: A contractor identifies work outside the original instruction and sends a quote. The account manager checks the contract scope, rate card, spend limit, budget and technical need while the site wants the job finished. Without a complete approval pack, chargeable work can begin before the client’s authorized decision is recorded.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks compares the proposed work with the contracted scope, pricing and approval limits, then prepares the variation pack. The technical manager confirms need and the client approves spend before the authorized variation or purchase order is recorded and communicated.

rightContent.quote: Extra work needs an approved scope, price and authority before it becomes a billable variation.

pages.eyebrow: 04 / Service response · Conflicting status to verified action
pages.title: Multi-system service exceptions
pages.problem: An urgent job is approaching its service deadline, but the client portal and provider’s FM system show different priorities, clock states and arrival times. The coordinator checks the contract, dispatch history, contractor acknowledgement and access arrangements. The duty manager needs a credible arrival commitment and an escalation decision while the site keeps calling.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks reconciles event history with the contract’s clock definitions and latest contractor confirmation. The duty manager approves escalation or alternative dispatch; agreed status updates are recorded, with disputed clock changes and service credits left to the client’s contract authority.

rightContent.alt: Facilities service van with ladders parked outside an office building

pages.eyebrow: 05 / Maintenance planning · Displaced visits to approved recovery
pages.title: Planned maintenance recovery
pages.problem: Emergency callouts and restricted access displace visits from the monthly maintenance plan. The planner compares work orders, rosters, attendance and service reports to establish what actually happened. A task may be done without proof or still unperformed, and critical inspections cannot simply move because the available crew has changed this week.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks reconciles planned visits with verified execution and identifies the missing evidence or recovery decision. The planner proposes the schedule; technical and HSE authorities assess critical deadlines, and the client confirms access before approved dates and escalations are recorded.

rightContent.quote: One significant obstacle to change is the siloed nature of data and teams

pages.eyebrow: 06 / Site access · Booked visit to authorized entry
pages.title: Contractor readiness
pages.problem: A contractor is available for the visit, but insurance, trade credentials, induction or the site’s permit requirements are missing or out of date. Procurement checks the vendor portal and emails the contractor while the site team checks access. The booking can still result in refused entry or work starting without the required clearance.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks assembles a site-specific readiness case and requests the exact credential or confirmation. Procurement and HSE review the evidence; site security or the responsible client authority approves entry and permits before the visit is confirmed or formally rescheduled.

rightContent.alt: Building permit posted on the fence of a construction site

beforeItems: Client portals, contractor replies and finance records disagree.

Each exception has a specific request, accountable owner and review point.
Client, technical, HSE and finance authorities approve their own decisions.
Accepted evidence and authorized outcomes return to the operational record.

pages.headline: Start with one completed job waiting to bill
pages.body: Choose a completed work order with an invoice or client-billing exception. We’ll map the scope, purchase order, service evidence and approval path with your account and finance teams. Agree the baseline and acceptance criteria, then demonstrate a verified billing disposition recorded in the existing workflow before extending the approach across sites and client contracts.
